what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat adults with a condition called generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), which is a disease that causes muscle weakness, and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP), which causes weakness and numbness in the arms and legs. It works by reducing certain harmful proteins in your blood called antibodies that are causing your immune system to attack your own body.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your belly (abdomen) or thigh. A healthcare provider will give you the injection in a clinic or doctor's office. Each injection session takes about 30 to 90 seconds. You will need to stay at the clinic for a short time after your injection so your healthcare team can make sure you feel okay. Do NOT inject this medicine yourself at home unless your doctor has specifically trained you to do so.
dosing: For myasthenia gravis (gMG): The usual dose is 1,000 mg given once a week for 4 weeks. This 4-week period is called a treatment cycle. Your doctor will check how you are doing and decide if you need another cycle of treatment. For CIDP: The usual starting dose is 1,000 mg given once a week for 4 weeks, followed by maintenance doses every 2 or 4 weeks depending on how you respond. Your doctor will determine the exact schedule that is right for you. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose and schedule.
missed_dose: If you miss or have to skip a scheduled injection appointment, call your doctor or healthcare provider as soon as possible to reschedule. Try not to miss appointments because staying on schedule is important for this medicine to work properly. Do not try to give yourself an extra dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. If you are given vials to bring to your appointment, keep them in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Do not freeze the medicine. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not shake the vials. If you have any questions about storing this medicine, ask your pharmacist or nurse.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while using this medicine, as it affects your immune system and live vaccines could cause infection. Talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines. Tell all of your doctors and dentists that you are on this medicine before any procedures or surgeries. Avoid being around people who are sick with infections, and wash your hands frequently. Avoid starting this medicine if you currently have a serious or active infection — talk to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness, or fast heartbeat; signs of infection such as fever, chills, cough, sore throat, burning with urination, or a wound that is red, swollen, or oozing; unusual weakness or worsening of your symptoms; chest tightness or shortness of breath; or any new or concerning symptoms. Contact your doctor if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant while on this medicine.
when_it_works: Some patients begin to notice improvement in their muscle strength or symptoms within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take longer for others to feel the full benefit. Because this medicine is given in cycles, your doctor will regularly evaluate how well it is working for you and adjust your treatment plan as needed. Do not be discouraged if you do not feel better right away — keep attending your appointments and talk to your doctor about how you are feeling.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe to use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, so you can discuss the risks and benefits together. Children: This medicine is currently approved only for adults and has not been studied in children under 18. Older adults: Older patients may use this medicine but should be monitored closely by their doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your doctor may need to monitor you more closely.
